claim: Asking the user the question with the highest expected information about the fault (entropy) needs far fewer oracle queries than halving the candidate set, when priors are informative; with poor priors the gain shrinks and a wrong fixed rule can cost 100-250% extra effort.
agent_test: Equal-token A/B: choose next check by estimated information gain over candidate faults vs fixed halving; count checks to isolate planted fault.

claim: Diagnosis search cost is dominated by a few hard conflict/consistency calls; reusing search state (DynamicHS, RBF-HS) cuts time and memory by large factors, but the gain is engineering, not reasoning quality.
agent_test: Not an agent test; informs only budget: keep candidate set small.

claim: Humans using interactive diagnosis tools make input errors and are overconfident: about a quarter gave at least one wrong answer, and mean confidence 83% vs 34% who found the true diagnosis. An oracle that can be wrong must be modelled.
agent_test: Inject 10-25% wrong answers into the oracle at equal tokens; compare agent that re-asks/cross-checks vs one that trusts.

claim: A model-based diagnosis tool helped spreadsheet debuggers in a small study: 100% vs 67% success and 163 s vs 547 s (N=24, one sheet, one fault).
agent_test: Give agent a spreadsheet with one injected fault, with and without a candidate-ranking helper; compare success at equal tokens.

claim: Coarse-to-fine localization works: fragment-level diagnosis cut cell-level diagnoses from 2,304 to 2 on a sheet, and added fragment tests isolated the cause in all 5 sheets. Update: an LLM reproduces coarse-to-fine localization; Agentless skeleton view 58.33% at $0.02 vs full file 53.67% at $0.15.
agent_test: Ask agent to localize to a block first, then a cell; compare to cell-by-cell.

claim: LLMs beat spectrum-based fault localization on real bugs when given tools/navigation, but explanations are often poor: 20% of AutoFL explanations accurate, 46.7% bland.
agent_test: Self-consistency across runs as confidence: merge top answers of k samples vs single sample at equal tokens.

claim: Gains from LLM fault localization are not just memorisation: leak-free StuDefects still gives 52.9% over state of the art, though class-level was worse than the baseline.
agent_test: Use freshly written faults when testing the agent.

claim: Intrinsic self-correction without external signal does not help and often hurts (GPT-3.5 CommonSenseQA 75.8 to 38.1; GPT-4 GSM8K 95.5 to 89.0); external feedback (tests, tools, stronger model, humans) is what lifts repair.
agent_test: Compare agent revising from own critique vs revising from a tool/test result at equal tokens; count right-to-wrong flips.

claim: Replacing LLM-based diagnosis with a solver-derived diagnosis plus an acceptance gate reduces right-to-wrong regressions (1.3% vs 11.8%) and raises accuracy (+8.7 pp over LLM diagnosis).
agent_test: Gate: accept a revision only if a checker confirms it fixes the failing check and breaks none passing.

claim: Verification-backed confidence is more informative than stated confidence: LLMs say at least 0.9 on 76.2% of answers, while counterfactual verification separates correct (93.6%) from the wrong third. Update: verbalized confidence is overconfident (Xiong 2024) and separates right from wrong poorly for 6 of 7 models on software artifacts (TRACE).
agent_test: Compare verbalized confidence vs check-based confidence as a trigger for re-open at equal tokens.

claim: Current LLM agents fail at spreadsheet debugging: best 12% on SpreadsheetBench 2 debugging (Claude Opus 4.6), error-value tasks barely above 20%; general SpreadsheetBench best near 18-20%. Fixing single errors does not give final pass (34% vs 3%).
agent_test: Add a final whole-task check; measure single-fix rate vs full pass.

claim: Benchmarks built from synthetic faults overstate real ability: FoRepBench execution match falls from 0.80 to 0.41 (GPT-4.1) on real seed set; SWE-bench Lite had 4.3% leaked patches, 10% missing info, 5% misleading.
agent_test: Test agent on real, not injected faults.

claim: Multi-step failure attribution is very hard for LLMs: best 53.5% agent-level, 14.2% step-level; worse with long context. Update: scaffolds lift step-level to 29-47% on Who&When (A2P), a coarse-to-fine hybrid raises step accuracy from 4.39 to 12.28% at about 9x tokens, and bisection does not help step accuracy.
agent_test: Give agent a long log with one bad step; test chunked search vs whole-log reading.

claim: Prompt formulation matters in spreadsheet error detection: Gemini 2.5 Pro found 12 of 12 seeded errors, small/cheap models 2-4, but results from one small test set with no repeats.
agent_test: Needs repeats before use.

claim: Reasoning-optimized models outperform general ones on knowledge-base consistency tasks (81.1% vs 61.0%), but slow large reasoners cost 500x runtime of a dedicated diagnosis algorithm (9,508 s vs 18.45 s).
agent_test: Delegate consistency checks to a solver tool when one exists.

claim: Reducing a hard diagnosis to a smaller sub-problem lets any MBD problem be handled as knowledge-base debugging; the same reduction is how LLM tasks (spreadsheet, spec, config) can reuse one repair loop.
agent_test: Theory; test by sharing one loop across task types.

claim: Tool design changes agent diagnosis: structured tool levels raised top-1 from 52.7% to 82.8%, but overrides of correct candidates outnumbered corrections.
schema_part: S5, G (do not override good candidate)
agent_test: Count how often agent drops a correct leading candidate after more evidence.

claim: Symbolic step verification improves detection of unfaithful reasoning (F1 70.7) and up to 4 repair rounds beat baselines.
agent_test: Limit repair rounds to 4 and compare.

claim: An LLM that scores candidate questions by expected information gain beats direct prompting on closed-set diagnosis games (UoT +38.1% relative; BED-LLM +37.4 points on 20 Questions). Only toy tasks with simulated, reliable answerers; no real-fault or equal-token test exists.
agent_test: Equal-token A/B on real faults: EIG-ranked probes vs free-form debugging.

claim: Executable external gates raise correct repairs: regression tests 77 to 81, plus reproduction tests 96 fixes on SWE-bench Lite; a solver diagnosis gate cuts regressions to 1.3%. Model-written checks are themselves often wrong (only 94 of 213 reproduction tests verified the true fix), so an independent second gate is needed.
agent_test: Accept a revision only if an independent check passes; log how often the model's own check disagrees with it.

claim: Hierarchical (coarse-to-fine) localization by an LLM cuts tokens and keeps accuracy; skipping levels hurts. In logs the hybrid uses about 9x the tokens of all-at-once.
agent_test: Compare file-function-line vs direct line search on token count and hit rate.

claim: LLMs trust prose over executed behaviour and are overconfident: doc faults found 67-94% but detection falls 21-43 points when only code changes; verbalized confidence separates right from wrong poorly.
agent_test: Weigh evidence by type; require an executed check before accepting a prose-based diagnosis.

claim: OPEN: no source measures how a 10-25% wrong-answer rate affects entropy-based probing versus re-ask strategies for LLM oracles. Only adjacent signals: BED-LLM notes entropy fails on noisy answers; 56% of LLM reproduction tests failed to verify a correct fix.
agent_test: Inject 10 and 25% wrong answers into a probe loop; compare entropy, EIG with a noise model, and re-ask.

claim: OPEN: no replication of the Jannach and Schmitz spreadsheet result (more sheets, fault types, practicing users) was found; search access was exhausted.
agent_test: Needs a literature pass with working search.

claim: OPEN: no source gives LLM results on spreadsheet error-value cases (#REF!, #NUM!) or tool-use patterns such as formula tracing; FLAME and SpreadsheetBench abstracts do not cover it.
agent_test: Build a small suite of error-value sheets; test with and without a dependency-graph tool.

claim: OPEN: multi-fault handling in LLM repair loops is untested directly; EDGE gives only qualitative gains for multi-error attribution.
agent_test: Plant two interacting faults; check whether the loop stops after the first fix.
